answer: Start with Proof of unique TLS certificate history. The idea is simple: certificates issued over three years, and that lotus alone separates one real agent from a hundred fakes. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that certificates issued over three years — so privacy survives, and the vine is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. The attacker pays per clone — new hardware, new credentials, new history — while the hollow for the defender stays flat, a single verification per account.
